1	There are a number of settings to allow you to configure OPTIMA Joystick to your exact requirements.
     2	These are all programmed using Learn Mode and are stored in an internal, non-volatile memory so they
     3	are automatically recalled each time you use the unit, even if you swap computers.
     4	To make changes to the settings, you must first go into Learn Mode. Press and hold the middle button
     5	until a warbling tone is heard. The unit is now in Learn Mode and is able to accept changes to the
     6	settings, as follows:
     7	Learn Mode
     8	Features
     9	• Plug and Play USB and PS/2 operation and requires no drivers.
    10	• PC, Mac and Chromebook compatible.
    11	• Switchable to Gaming output for full compatibility
    12	 with Xbox Adaptive Controller
    13	• Light touch joystick movement.
    14	• User-selectable cursor speed settings.
    15	• Drag lock and double click features.
    16	• Sockets to operate left and right click from remote switches.
    17	• Robust construction and ergonomic design.
    18	• Industry-standard mounting option.
    19	• Optional left-handed operation.
    20	Cursor Speed
    21	To change the speed setting while in Learn Mode, press the middle button briefly. Each time you do
    22	so, the unit emits a number of beeps, between 1 and 4. One beep indicates the lowest speed and 4 the
    23	highest. The speed of the cursor changes immediately, allowing you to experiment until the best
    24	setting is found.
    25	Left-Handed Operation
    26	The left and right buttons may be swapped around, which is particularly useful for left-landed
    27	users. To change this setting, press the left button while in Learn Mode. One beep indicates the
    28	unit is set to standard ‘right-handed’ mode, whereas two beeps indicates ‘left-handed’ operation.
    29	Double Click
    30	Right-click may be substituted with Double-Click, which is useful for users who have difficulty in
    31	double-clicking quickly enough for the computer to recognise. To change this setting, press the
    32	right button briefly while in Learn Mode. One beep indicates the unit is set to standard
    33	‘right-click’ mode, whereas two beeps indicates ‘Double-Click’ operation.
    34	Buzzer On/Off
    35	OPTIMA Joystick is fitted with a buzzer which gives an audible indication of operations such as drag
    36	lock and unlock, double-click, entering Learn Mode etc. When OPTIMA Joystick is used in a classroom
    37	setting, where there may be many units in close proximity, it may be beneficial to turn off the
    38	buzzer. To achieve this, press and hold the right button while in Learn Mode, until two long beeps
    39	are heard. The buzzer is now disabled, although it will still operate while in Learn Mode. Repeating
    40	the above operation will re-enable it.
    41	All of the above settings may be changed as often as required while in Learn Mode, allowing you to
    42	experiment with the settings until the best configuration is found. Once you are happy with the
    43	settings, they may be stored in the non-volatile memory by pressing and holding the middle button
    44	once again, until the warbling tone is heard. Normal operation then resumes. Note that if both
    45	left-handed operation and Double-Click are selected, the buttons will function
    46	as Double-Click, Drag and Left Click, reading from left to right. Also note that the function of the
    47	sockets for external switches reproduces the function of the
    48	internal buttons, according to the above settings. The unit automatically leaves Learn Mode, and any
    49	changes are discarded, if the settings remain unchanged for more than a minute.

Looking at the document, I need to work through each requested change on a **new device** (i.e., at factory defaults: standard right-handed mode, lowest cursor speed, standard right-click, buzzer on):

1. **Right-handed operation** — The document states the unit's standard mode is 'right-handed' (one beep indicates right-handed, two beeps left-handed). A new device is already in right-handed mode, so no button press is needed → **0 beeps**.

2. **Cursor speed to 2** — "Each time you do so, the unit emits a number of beeps, between 1 and 4. One beep indicates the lowest speed..." A new device starts at the lowest speed (1). Pressing the middle button once to raise it to speed 2 → **2 beeps**.

3. **Double click** — "One beep indicates the unit is set to standard 'right-click' mode, whereas two beeps indicates 'Double-Click' operation." A new device is in standard right-click mode, so one press of the right button → **2 beeps**.

4. **Buzzer off** — "Press and hold the right button while in Learn Mode, until two long beeps are heard. The buzzer is now disabled" → **2 beeps**.

(Entering and exiting Learn Mode produce a "warbling tone," not beeps, so those don't count.)

**Total: 0 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 beeps.**
